runs.content: Thursday's rotation focus is Books + Podcasts. Since the last thinker run (2026-09-15, Tuesday), a scheduler outage blocked most scheduled tasks on 09-16 and 09-17 (see memory/mcp_local_servers_connect_timeout_2026_09_15) — the only genuinely new material this week was the 2026-09-15 book-recommender's September batch in books/suggestions.md; Podcasts had no new pages or recommendations at all. Both findings today trace back to that single new batch. Investigation idea: the batch recommends Sorkin's '1929' explicitly because it 'lands squarely on his live AI-capex-bubble tracking (Djukanovic, Klement, Grantham)' — but checking those pages shows the fit is thinner than the recommendation implies: ai-tech/source-ai-supremacy-compute-demand-disrupt-america-2026-08-10.md cites 1929 as only one number in a margin-debt checklist, and finance/investor-letters/source-djukanovic-ai-capital-cycle-2026-06-26.md reaches for the 1873 Panic of the railroads, not 1929, as its historical anchor — none of the wiki's AI-bubble pages actually work through 1929's own credit/margin-call mechanics the way Sorkin's Fed-minutes-sourced book would. Cross-domain connection: the same batch's 'Rise of the Machines' (drone warfare, Ukraine) recommendation independently names both finance/ideas/idea-rheinmetall.md and technology/source-guardian-fire-point-ukraine-missiles-2026-07-27.md in its own 'Why Fred' text — the identical unlinked pair a 2026-08-01 thinker entry already flagged as open. That the book-recommender's own reasoning (built from reading history, not from reading either page) independently rediscovers the same gap from a different domain and a different automated process is a second, distinct signal it's real. Neither book is ingested yet (recommendations only) — both concrete next steps start with adding them to reading-list.md's aspirational section. Checked the open sections for resolution: nothing showed clear signs of being actioned since 2026-09-15.

Tuesday's rotation focus is AI & Tech + Technology. Since the last thinker run (2026-09-14, Monday), log.md's top-of-file section showed only two routine Finance tracker updates (sector-performance-tracker, book-recommender) — but a deeper check of file modification times turned up a substantial, unlogged-at-top evening session on 2026-09-14: a clippings-sorter run processed 7 clippings, including two new Michael Burry trading posts, four Citrini 'Global Macro Trading for Idiots' pages, and one AI & Tech clipping — Kakashii's skeptical line-by-line annotation of the April 2026 Dwarkesh x Jensen Huang interview. That single new AI & Tech page turned up two genuinely new findings. Investigation idea: Kakashii's point 4 argues the GPU shortage ended in late 2024 and Nvidia has been in an oversupply regime since (GPUs sitting unassigned in warehouses) — a live, present-tense dispute against the dominant supply-constrained narrative built up across ai-tech/data-hbm-supply-chain-2026-06-27.md ('sold out through 2026-2027') and ai-tech/model-ai-ecosystem-constraint-edges-2026-06-27.md (CoWoS/TSMC as binding chokepoint), both of which only model oversupply as a theoretical 2027+ bear case, not something already happening at the GPU level today. Cross-domain connection: the Kakashii page explicitly states its neocloud-demand-engineering argument is 'structurally the same argument Burry makes about off-balance-sheet AI financing' and links twice to finance/michael-burry/index.md — but that Finance hub page, updated in the very same ingestion session with two new trading posts and an active NVDA short, has no reverse link back (a grep for 'kakashii' in the file returns nothing), unlike the Kakashii page's other cross-link (to the neutral Dwarkesh-Jensen episode notes), which the same run did make bidirectional. Checked the open sections for resolution: nothing showed clear signs of being actioned since 2026-09-14.
